rationale.Atorvastatin / Rosuvastatin: Guidelines recommend high-intensity statins (Rosuvastatin 20-40 mg or Atorvastatin 40-80 mg) for ACS. Simvastatin is not high-intensity even at max dose.
rationale.Beta-blocker (Metoprolol / Atenolol): Metoprolol or atenolol are the preferred agents for treating MI. Oral preferred over IV.
rationale.Ticagrelor / Clopidogrel: Dual antiplatelet therapy is standard for NSTEMI patients without contraindications. Ticagrelor and Prasugrel preferred over Clopidogrel.
rationale.Consult, cardiology / Angioplasty with s: Cardiology should be consulted. PCI with stent placement is the preferred reperfusion treatment for NSTEMI.
rationale.Heparin, therapy: For NSTEMI, unfractionated heparin, enoxaparin, bivalirudin, or fondaparinux help prevent ischemic events.
rationale.Reteplase / Alteplase / Tenecteplase (Fi: Patients with Unstable angina or NSTEMI do NOT benefit from fibrinolysis. This is a critical distinction from STEMI management.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is an elderly woman with a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension who presents to the emergency department with progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and dizziness. She denies chest pain. The dyspnea has been gradual in onset, associated with lightheadedness but no fever, cough, palpitations, or orthopnea. Given her cardiovascular risk factors and atypical presentation — ST depression in leads I, II, V4-V6 suggesting subendocardial ischemia — acute coronary syndrome must be ruled out urgently.

physical_exam: Patient appears dyspneic and fatigued. Assess severity of illness and work of breathing.
Heart exam indicated for cardiac etiology. Assess for murmurs, rubs, gallops, JVD.
Chest and lung exam indicated for shortness of breath. Assess for crackles, wheezes, diminished breath sounds.

chief_complaint: Shortness of breath and fatigue with dizziness
case_summary: Atypical NSTEMI in elderly woman with DM and HTN. No chest pain — presents with dyspnea and fatigue. ST depression I, II, V4-V6 = subendocardial ischemia. Tx: PCI + DAPT + anticoagulation + beta-blocker + statin. Fibrinolysis contraindicated.
